chosen_plan_breakdown.about: the 12 largest contributions to the sung time with rub above -6 dB in the chosen plan. Only rows where a band note of the neighbouring pitch class is really struck are semitone coincidences; the others are overtones of consonant notes (the 5th harmonic of the bass D2 = F#4 under a sung F, the 3rd harmonic of B2 = F#4 under a sung G) and attack noise.

about: Audio check on rendered band audio (pitched accompaniment only, FluidSynth, settings of build.py): how much band energy lies one semitone from the sung pitch while the voice sings. rub level = power in the two semitone bands (+-50 cents) next to the sung pitch, same octave, in dB relative to one chord note of a strum (peak of the E4 band in the first off-beat strum of the verse). Shares are fractions of the sung time of the named stretch; runs follow the 150 ms rule of olcum.json. L2_and_L4_whole_bars = verse bars 2 and 6; beat_2_only = beat position 1.9 .. 2.95 of those bars (F on the beat, E on the off-beat); beat_3_only = 2.95 .. 4.0 (F E D). The semitone bands also catch the attack noise of every strum, so levels below about -12 dB are not evidence of a sounding note; the -6 dB rows are the robust ones.

band_level_time_course.about: RMS of the E4, F4 and D4 semitone bands in 1/8-beat steps through verse bars 2 and 6, dB re the strum note

not_verified_by_ear: This is a measurement of spectral energy next to the sung pitch; nobody listened.
